key_insight: EventHub is a data factory that enables training generalizable event-based stereo networks using only standard RGB images by generating proxy depth annotations and proxy events via novel view synthesis, removing the need for costly active-sensor ground truth.
problem_solved: Reduces dependence on expensive, hard-to-acquire active-sensor (e.g., LiDAR) annotations for event-based stereo learning, enabling scalable training data for event cameras and repurposing RGB stereo models for event-based tasks.
method: Generate training sets from ordinary color images by producing proxy depth annotations and synthesizing proxy events using state-of-the-art novel view synthesis and image-based rendering.
When image-event pairs exist, derive only proxy annotations and combine with real events; otherwise synthesize both events and annotations from images.
Use the generated datasets to train or fine-tune existing state-of-the-art stereo networks for event-based stereo tasks without relying on active-sensor ground truth.
impact: Makes event-based stereo research more accessible and scalable by removing the active-sensor bottleneck, accelerating development and deployment of event-camera depth estimation in robotics, autonomous systems, and low-light/high-dynamic-range scenarios.

paper_title: EventHub: Data Factory for Generalizable Event-Based Stereo Networks without Active Sensors
paper_authors: Luca Bartolomei, Fabio Tosi, Matteo Poggi, Stefano Mattoccia, Guillermo Gallego
